Transitory

/TRAN-sih-tor-ee/ - the stress falls on TRAN · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Transitory means lasting only a short time; not permanent.

The raise gave morale only a transitory lift; by spring the old grumbling was back.

Worked Example

Jet lag is misery with a guarantee. The fog, the 3 a.m. hunger, the noon crash — every bit of it is transitory, burning off as the body's clock slides into the new zone at roughly a sunrise per day. Travelers who understand this simply wait it out; the condition was never built to last, and in three mornings it is gone.

Transitory is the exact word because it names what lasts only a short time and is not permanent — a state already on its way out. It does not demand speed: a transitory phase may take a season to pass. The word's quiet comfort, and its quiet warning, are the same sentence: it will not stay.

How Transitory Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

impermanent

impermanent: the flat denial of permanence

short-term

short-term: planned to be brief — businesslike, no poetry

Antonyms

long-lasting

long-lasting: built to stay for years on end

here-to-stay

here-to-stay: settled in for good

How Strong Is It? — impermanent → transitory → vanishing

impermanent vs. transitory

impermanent vs. transitory: Impermanent states only that a thing will not last forever; transitory adds that it is already moving through, a phase on its way out.

vanishing vs. transitory

vanishing vs. transitory: Vanishing goes past transitory — dissolving even as you name it, with no season of passage at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — trans-

Prefix — trans-: across

Root — it

Root — it: to go (Latin ire)

Suffix — -ory

Suffix — -ory: characterized by

Put it together

Put it together: Trans- (across) + it (to go) + -ory (characterized by) = characterized by going across. Latin transire meant to pass over or pass through, and transitory keeps the traveler in view: whatever it describes is in transit through your life, crossing on its way to somewhere else.

Use the root in a new word: exit

Use the root in a new word: exit: The theater's exit is, quite literally, the way one goes out.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / reflective

Transitory denies permanence without insisting on speed — it suits phases and conditions that will pass in their own time. Its cluster-mates in this unit go further: ephemeral squeezes a whole life into a day, and momentary into an instant. For an arrangement with a posted end date, plain temporary is the businesslike choice.
